question: In Java's single inheritance model, how many direct superclasses can a concrete class extend?

options.text: Up to two direct superclasses if one is abstract.
As many as desired using comma-separated class names in the extends clause.
Exactly one direct superclass.
Zero, because all classes must directly descend from java.lang.Object only.

explanation: Java allows a class to extend exactly one direct superclass, enforcing a tree-structured class inheritance hierarchy.

question: Which relationship does the `extends` keyword model between classes in Java?

options.text: An IS-A relationship: the subclass is a specialized type of the superclass.
A detached relationship: opting out of superclass constructor invocation.
A HAS-A relationship: the superclass contains instances of the subclass.
A SIBLING relationship: two classes can be used interchangeably anywhere.

explanation: Class inheritance in Java represents an IS-A relationship. A subclass inherits state and behaviors from its superclass and can be treated as a superclass type.

question: What is the result when evaluating `(subclassInstance instanceof Object)` for any valid non-null Java object?

options.text: It always evaluates to true because every Java object is an instance of Object.
It throws ClassCastException unless the instance is explicitly downcast.
It evaluates to false unless the class explicitly declares extends Object.
It evaluates to true only for classes implementing java.io.Serializable.

explanation: Because java.lang.Object is the ultimate ancestor of all classes, any non-null object reference is guaranteed to evaluate to true with instanceof Object.

question: Is downcasting a superclass reference to a subclass type always safe at runtime?

options.text: No, downcasting is strictly forbidden and rejected at compile time in Java.
No, downcasting succeeds at runtime only if the actual object is an instance of that subclass.
Yes, downcasting is always safe as long as the superclass constructor is invoked.
Yes, downcasting is always safe because subclasses inherit all members from the superclass.

explanation: Downcasting requires an explicit cast and is checked at runtime. If the underlying heap object is not an instance of the target subclass, a ClassCastException is thrown.

question: Can private members of a superclass be directly accessed by name inside a subclass method?

options.text: Yes, downcasting the superclass reference automatically exposes all private fields.
Yes, because superclass constructors grant direct field access to subclasses.
Yes, provided the subclass resides in the same package as sibling classes.
No, private members are not accessible outside the declaring class body.

explanation: Private members of a superclass are not visible in subclasses. Subclasses can access them only indirectly through public or protected methods.
